claims.quote: the swift aeroplane, with its atomic engine as noiseless as a dancing sunbeam and its phosphorescent gyroscopic compass, flew like an arrow to the heart of the Central European hosts.
claims.description: Aircraft powered by silent atomic engines, guided by a phosphorescent gyroscopic compass.

claims.quote: the new bombs that would continue to explode indefinitely and which no one so far had ever seen in action.
claims.description: Atomic bombs that keep exploding continuously rather than in a single instant.

claims.quote: Carolinum, which belonged to the β-Group of Hyslop’s so-called ‘suspended degenerator’ elements, once its degenerative process had been induced, continued a furious radiation of energy and nothing could arrest it.
claims.description: An artificial radioactive element that, once triggered, releases enormous energy continuously and cannot be stopped.

claims.quote: it poured out half of the huge store of energy in its great molecules in the space of seventeen days, the next seventeen days’ emission was a half of that first period’s outpouring, and so on.
claims.description: An artificial element with a 17-day half-life that releases its energy by exponential decay.

claims.quote: to this day the battle-fields and bomb fields of that frantic time in human history are sprinkled with radiant matter, and so centres of inconvenient rays.
claims.description: Lingering radioactive contamination of battlefields long after atomic bombing.

claims.quote: Those that were thrown from aeroplanes fell in this state, they reached the ground still mainly solid, and, melting soil and rock in their progress, bored into the earth.
claims.description: Atomic bombs dropped from aircraft burrow into the ground and form erupting, volcano-like craters of fiery energy.

claims.quote: Never before in the history of warfare had there been a continuing explosive
claims.description: A new kind of weapon, a continuing explosive, unlike all earlier momentary explosives.

claims.quote: Before the last war began it was a matter of common knowledge that a man could carry about in a handbag an amount of latent energy sufficient to wreck half a city.
claims.description: Portable devices containing enough atomic energy to destroy half a city.

claims.quote: Destruction was becoming so facile that any little body of malcontents could use it; it was revolutionising the problems of police and internal rule.
claims.description: Cheap and easy destructive power lets small groups of malcontents wreak havoc, upending policing and governance.

claims.quote: nothing could have been more obvious to the people of the earlier twentieth century than the rapidity with which war was becoming impossible.
claims.description: Increasing destructive power makes major war impossible.

claims.quote: Collective civilisation, the ‘Modern State,’ was still in the womb of the future....
claims.description: A future organised collective political order, the 'Modern State', will replace the aimless social organisation of the era.

claims.quote: The Labour Bureaux were now partially transformed into enrolment offices, and were centres of hotly patriotic excitement.
claims.description: A future general European war pitting the Allies (France, Britain, Slavs) against the Central European powers, with troop trains running through a Channel Tunnel.

claims.quote: At every convenient place upon the line on either side of the Channel Tunnel there were enthusiastic spectators
claims.description: A railway tunnel under the English Channel carrying troop trains.

claims.quote: the formation of an aerial park in this region, from which attacks could be made upon the vast industrial plant of the lower Rhine
claims.description: Large aerial bases launching air attacks on enemy industrial areas.

claims.quote: the reports of the British Admiralty and of the Slav commanders were recorded as they kept coming to hand.
claims.description: A centralised war control room in Paris coordinating the whole war with wireless reports and large relief maps.

claims.quote: Delhi might talk of a great flank march through Holland, with all the British submarines and hydroplanes and torpedo craft pouring up the Rhine in support of it
claims.description: Flotillas of submarines, hydroplanes and torpedo craft supporting an offensive up the Rhine.

claims.quote: Viard might crave for brilliance with the motor bicycles, aeroplanes, and ski-men among the Swiss mountains
claims.description: Mobile warfare using motor bicycles, aeroplanes and ski troops in the Alps.
Aerial atomic bombing destroys the Paris war headquarters and then the Berlin imperial headquarters.
claims.stated_time: the night of July the second
